title: Mortgage Pre-Approval Issuance Standard
content:
A Mortgage Pre-Approval is issued at the level the borrower requested, with a maximum loan amount, a maximum purchase price and an expiration date, only once that level's checks and tests are met.

## Section 1. Checks before issue

1.1 A pre-approval is issued only after the level's checks: the credit pull of the level's credit inquiry type, with the borrower's recorded consent where the level requires consent to a hard credit inquiry to be recorded; income and assets reviewed where the level reviews income documents and asset statements; automated findings where the level requires automated underwriting findings to be run; and underwriter sign-off where the level requires an underwriter to sign the approval.

## Section 2. Qualification tests

2.1 The target loan program must be among the level's eligible loan programs, the credit score at least the level's minimum credit score, and the planned down payment at least the level's minimum planned down payment.

2.2 The credit score is the representative credit score from the credit report the pre-approval rests on. The planned down payment is the down payment the borrower plans, as a percent of the purchase price. The target loan program is the loan program the pre-approval is sized for.

Boundary illustration, using a hypothetical minimum score of 600 and a hypothetical minimum down payment of 5.00 percent (example figures only):

| Test | Met when | Just met | Just not met |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credit score | at least the minimum | score 600 | score 599 |
| Planned down payment | at least the minimum | 5.00 percent | 4.99 percent |
| Target loan program | among the level's eligible programs | program listed for the level | program not listed for the level |

## Section 3. Maximum loan amount

3.1 The maximum loan amount is the largest base loan whose payment, at the current rate-sheet rate plus the level's rate buffer, with property taxes at the level's property tax assumption, keeps debt-to-income at the target program's maximum debt-to-income ratio less the level's debt-to-income cushion, capped at the program's loan limit.

3.2 Read as its parts: the payment is calculated at a rate equal to the current rate-sheet rate with the level's buffer points added; property taxes in that payment are the level's annual assumption as a percent of the price; the debt-to-income the loan must keep to is the program's maximum less the level's cushion points; and where the largest base loan meeting that debt-to-income is above the program's loan limit, the maximum loan amount is the program's loan limit.

Hypothetical illustration: with a rate-sheet rate of 6.500 percent and a buffer of 0.250 points, the payment is sized at 6.750 percent; with a program maximum of 45.00 percent and a cushion of 2.00 points, the debt-to-income kept to is 43.00 percent. If the largest base loan meeting that debt-to-income were USD 820,000 under a program loan limit of USD 806,500, the maximum loan amount would be USD 806,500; if it were USD 610,000 under the same limit, it would be USD 610,000. All figures are example inputs.

## Section 4. Maximum purchase price

4.1 The maximum purchase price is the maximum loan amount divided by one minus the down payment fraction, rounded down to the level's rounding increment. The down payment fraction is the planned down payment percentage expressed as a fraction, that is, the percentage divided by one hundred.

Worked example on hypothetical inputs: maximum loan amount USD 361,250 and a planned down payment of 10.00 percent. The down payment fraction is 0.10; one minus 0.10 is 0.90; USD 361,250 divided by 0.90 is USD 401,388.89. Rounded down to a hypothetical increment of USD 1,000 the maximum purchase price is USD 401,000; rounded down to a hypothetical increment of USD 5,000 it is USD 400,000. Rounding is always down, never to the nearest increment.

## Section 5. Expiration date

5.1 The expiration date is the issued date plus the level's validity in calendar days. It is the last day the pre-approval and its letters are valid.

Hypothetical illustration: a pre-approval issued on 1 March at a level with a validity of 90 calendar days has an expiration date of 30 May.

## Section 6. Decline and fee

6.1 A borrower who fails the checks is declined; there is no fee for the pre-approval.

6.2 A request either is issued at the requested level or is declined where the borrower does not qualify at any amount for the level. Every check of Section 1 and every test of Section 2 met: the pre-approval is issued. Any one of them not met: the borrower is declined.
